forms: recall a fact of the parable
say why the third servant was blamed
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..mastery: Says that the master gave five, two and one talents, each according to ability; that the first two servants used theirs and gained more; that the third buried his; that the master praised the faithful servants; and that the lesson is to use what God has given. Does not read the talents as only money or say the master was unfair. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match a verse to its message
choose the response that fits the verse
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..mastery: Says that God has plans for the child's welfare, future and hope (Jeremiah 29:11), that every good gift comes from God (James 1:17) and that each person should use the gift received to serve others (1 Peter 4:10). Does not say that gifts are for showing off or only for adults. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: a role at home, school or church
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.mastery: Names the responsibilities in Genesis 1:26 and 2:15 (rule over, look after, till and keep the garden) and tells caring for creation from using it up. Gives roles a child really has at home, at school and at church. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.mastery: Separates child labour (work that is heavy, harmful, or keeps a child from school) from light chores that suit a child's age; gives causes (poverty, ignorance, greed of employers, loss of parents) and effects (missing school, harm to health, loss of play and safety); and names safe people to report to (a parent or guardian, a teacher, the chief, a children's officer or the Childline Kenya helpline 116). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.mastery: Says that the serpent tempted the woman, that she and the man ate from the tree God had forbidden, that they hid when they heard God, and that God asked "Where are you?"; and states lessons: obey God, do not blame others, wrong choices have results. Does not say the Bible names the fruit. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.mastery: Gives reasons family unity matters (love, help, peace, safety), names challenges families face (quarrels, poverty, illness, long absence, unkind words), and gives ways a child helps (forgiving, doing chores, speaking kindly, obeying). Knows that Colossians 3:13-14 speaks of bearing with one another, forgiving and love. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.mastery: Gives uses of the Bible in society (teaching right and wrong, comfort, guidance, worship, prayer, oaths on some occasions, moral teaching in schools) and benefits of reading it (growing in faith, wisdom, strength, direction). Knows that Joshua 1:8 and Psalm 1:1-3 speak of meditating on God's word and its blessing. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..mastery: Says that Peter and John were arrested for teaching about Jesus, were questioned about the power by which a man had been healed, that Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke boldly, that he said there is salvation in no other name than Jesus (Acts 4:12), and that the rulers saw their courage and knew they had been with Jesus. Gives a reason to stand firm. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
a lesson or a wise choice
CRES.G5.THE_BI.KING_SOLOMON_THE_WISE_RU..mastery: Says that two women claimed one living baby, that Solomon called for a sword to divide the child, that the real mother gave up her claim to save the child, and that Solomon gave the baby to her. Gives lessons (wisdom, listening to both sides, love shows in giving) and what Proverbs 9:10 says. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G5.THE_BI.NOAH_AND_HIS_SONS.NOAH_SO.mastery: Names Shem, Ham and Japheth as the sons of Noah who came out of the ark; says that Noah planted a vineyard, drank wine and lay uncovered in his tent; that Ham told his brothers; and that Shem and Japheth covered their father without looking. Does not mix up the sons with other Bible brothers. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: what to do in a situation
CRES.G5.THE_BI.NOAH_AND_HIS_SONS.RESPECT.mastery: Gives ways of showing respect to older people (greeting politely, listening, helping with loads and chores, giving a seat, speaking kindly, visiting) and does not think respect means agreeing with everything or only applies to relatives. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.THE_BI.A_HAND_WRITES_ON_THE_WAL..mastery: Says that King Belshazzar held a feast and used the gold and silver vessels from the temple in Jerusalem, that a human hand wrote on the wall, that no wise man could read it, that Daniel was called and read it, and that the writing said the kingdom had been counted, weighed and divided. Gives lessons (do not misuse holy things, pride has a price, God is above kings). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

Describes humility as thinking rightly of yourself and others, without boasting; gives benefits (peace, learning, friends, honour from God and people) and tells Daniel's quiet, faithful service from the proud king's behaviour. Does not say that humility means being weak or having no opinion. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the contest
CRES.G5.THE_BI.MOUNT_CARMEL_CONTEST.CARM.mastery: Says that Elijah stood alone against 450 prophets of Baal, that each side prepared a bull and no one lit the fire, that Baal did not answer, that Elijah prayed and the fire of the Lord fell, and that the people said the Lord is God. Gives lessons (worship God alone, trust in prayer, courage to stand alone). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: what to do when invited to a harmful group
CRES.G5.THE_BI.MOUNT_CARMEL_CONTEST.TRUE.mastery: Tells the Lord who answered by fire from idols that cannot hear, see or speak; knows that the Ten Commandments forbid worshipping other gods and making idols to bow down to; and chooses a safe response when a group or friend invites a child to worship or follow something against these teachings. Never judges other people by name. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIRTH_OF_MOSES.MOSES_.mastery: Says that Moses' mother hid him for three months, put him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile, that his sister watched, that Pharaoh's daughter found him and took pity, that his own mother was paid to nurse him, and that he was named Moses. Gives lessons (God protects, courage of a mother, kindness to a stranger). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the call
how a leader obeys God today
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_CALL_OF_MOSES.MOSES_C.mastery: Says that Moses was looking after the flock when he saw a bush that burned without burning up, that God told him to take off his sandals because the ground was holy, that God had seen the people's suffering, and that Moses was sent to bring them out of Egypt. Gives lessons and ways Christian leaders obey God today. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CRES.G5.THE_LI.JOHN_THE_BAPTIST.JOHN_BAP.mastery: Says that John preached repentance and baptism, that he told the crowd to share spare clothing and food, told tax collectors to collect no more than was due, and told soldiers not to take money by force or accuse falsely and to be content with their pay. Gives lessons (repent, share, be honest, be content). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall an event at the baptism
CRES.G5.THE_LI.THE_BAPTISM_OF_JESUS_CHR..mastery: Says that Jesus was baptised and was praying, that heaven opened, that the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and that a voice from heaven called him the beloved Son. Gives the meaning Christians agree on (a sign of repentance, new life and belonging to God) without saying how or at what age baptism should be done. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the miracle
what to do in a challenge
CRES.G5.THE_LI.CALMING_THE_STORM.CALMING.mastery: Says that a great storm came while Jesus slept in the boat, that the disciples woke him and asked if he did not care, that Jesus told the wind and waves to be still and there was a great calm. Gives lessons (Jesus has power over nature, trust in God in trouble) and challenges Christians face. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the miracle
a way of helping the needy
CRES.G5.THE_LI.FEEDING_THE_FOUR_THOUSAN..mastery: Says that the crowd had been with Jesus three days, that Jesus had compassion, that there were seven loaves and a few small fish, that all ate and seven baskets were left, and does not mix it with the feeding of five thousand. Gives four ways of helping needy people today. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.THE_LI.HEALING_THE_PARALYSED_MA..mastery: Says that four friends carried the man, that the crowd blocked the door so they made an opening in the roof, that Jesus saw their faith and first said that the man's sins were forgiven. Gives lessons (faith in action, friends who help, pray when in trouble). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the parable
CRES.G5.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_SHEE..mastery: Says that the shepherd had a hundred sheep and one was lost, that he left the ninety-nine to look for it, carried it home on his shoulders, called friends to rejoice, and that Jesus said there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents. Gives lessons (God cares for each person, we should reach out to those who are lost). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match the virtue to its promise
choose the action that shows the virtue
CRES.G5.THE_LI.SERMON_ON_THE_MOUNT.SERMO.mastery: Says what Jesus promised to the merciful (they will receive mercy), the pure in heart (they will see God) and the peacemakers (they will be called children of God), and chooses the action that applies each virtue to school and home. Does not say a peacemaker is someone who never disagrees. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the story
CRES.G5.THE_LI.THE_RICH_YOUNG_MAN.RICH_Y.mastery: Says that the young man asked what good thing to do to have eternal life, that Jesus pointed him to the commandments, that the young man said he had kept them, that Jesus told him to sell what he had, give to the poor and follow him, and that he went away sad because he had great wealth. Gives lessons (put God first, share, wealth can hold the heart). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall a fact of the parable
CRES.G5.THE_LI.A_FRIEND_AT_MIDNIGHT.FRIE.mastery: Says that a man went to a friend at midnight to ask for three loaves for a visitor, that the friend first refused because the door was shut and the children were in bed, that he got up and gave because the man kept asking, and that Jesus taught ask, seek and knock. Gives the lesson of persistence in prayer. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: a value that keeps a church united
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.mastery: Lists what the believers devoted themselves to (the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayer), says that they shared what they owned with anyone in need and met daily with glad hearts, and names values that keep a church united (love, sharing, forgiveness, humility, respect). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: recall an event of the supper
a value for the Lord's Table
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.mastery: Says that Jesus sat with the apostles at the Passover meal, took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, took the cup, and told them to do this in remembrance of him; knows that churches use different names (Lord's Supper, Lord's Table, Holy Communion, Eucharist) for the same remembrance, and that reverence, thankfulness and forgiving others are values to bring to it.
